export.title: Export Icon Font
export.description: Export icon fonts so you can reference icons by code point or class name in web pages.
export.icpMigrationHint: You can now save .icp files independently — no need to include them in every export.
export.wikiLink: Learn about font formats in the Wiki
export.fmt.svg: XML-based vector font — human-readable, useful for debugging. Deprecated in most browsers, used as pipeline source format.
export.fmt.ttf: Universal binary font — works on all platforms. Ideal for desktop apps and OS-level font installation.
export.fmt.woff2: Best web format — Brotli-compressed, 30% smaller than WOFF. Supported by 97%+ browsers. Recommended for all web projects.
export.fmt.css: Generated @font-face rules + icon CSS classes. Drop into your project to use icons by class name.
export.fmt.woff: Web font with zlib compression — fallback for IE 11. Skip if you don't need legacy IE support.
export.fmt.eot: Microsoft proprietary format — IE 6–8 only. Skip unless targeting extremely legacy systems.
export.fmt.js: SVG symbol sprite — supports multi-color icons and individual animation. Alternative to font-based approach.
export.includeCssDesc: @font-face rules and icon CSS classes for web usage

projectSettings.coveragePuaHelp: Icon fonts map each icon to a Unicode code point. To avoid clashing with real text, the convention is to use the Private Use Area (PUA, U+E000–U+F8FF) — a range Unicode permanently reserves for private use, where no standard character will ever appear. It holds 6,400 code points, which is why the code limit is 6,400.
